values: Observations carry no feature of interest; they reach the machine through the sensor and the own property am:isAttachedToMachine. sosa:Sensor and sosa:Actuator are declared subclasses of an own am:Device class to keep OWL 2 RL.

Observations subclassed per property instance (irrig:Soil30cmDepthMoistureObservation…). caso:Observation marks aggregations with prov:wasInformedBy to its inputs, caso:Deduction gives a caso:State as result.
A DUL-aligned pattern network: observations express states (se-situ:State) and situations; a configuration procedure (subclass of sosa:Procedure) per sensor; TBox only, no instance data shown.
Sample chain in the case study: a sampling of room air gives the sample air, which is then the feature of interest of the observation. Adds own DeviceId and hasSubDevice to the SSN classes.
Deployments stand for areas of a laboratory (ssn:WestSideMaldiTof), and the work mints its own individuals in the ssn: namespace (ssn:SN_22, ssn:DHT22_22).

Alignment axioms only (SOSA to PROV-O, OBOE, BCO/OBI/BFO), no instance data. oboe:Measurement is made equivalent to sosa:Observation and an OBOE observation groups measurements through rdfs:member; ssn:Property is aligned to bfo:Quality.

SOSA properties are borrowed onto own classes bfp:Observation and bfp:Record (a device status), with no sosa:Observation or sosa:Sensor; devices link to their observations by own bfp:hasObservation / bfp:hasRecord.
SWRL privacy rules over observations, which are matched to terms of service by an own string observation_name and given data categories and privacy rules.
New relations are minted in the sosa namespace (sosa:close, sosa:hasSpatial, sosa:hasTemporal) and inferred by SWRL rules; reconstructed values are a subclass of sosa:Observation.
Collection-level metadata: properties set on an ObservationCollection (result, feature of interest) are shared by its members; the feature of interest comes from an external vocabulary (OIEAU).
The IotStream is the root node that carries sensor, quantity kind, unit, location and quality, so stream observations stay minimal; observations can be outputs of an analytics process.
Observations of virtual and cognitive sensors carry inferred results (activity levels, disease names) about an apartment, chained by stream reasoning.

Measurement samples (DICMeasurementSample, a subclass of sosa:Sample) are the entry point from which observations and results are reached; calibration outputs are linked to procedures with prov:wasGeneratedBy.

Instance IRIs are written under SOSA-like prefixes (sosa:Observation/…, sosa:Sensor/DHT11); each observation carries a blockchain hash and a trustability score, and SHACL shapes check observation quality.
IoT-Lite over SSN 2011 terms (ssn:Sensor, ssn:Device): no observation is modelled, sensors carry quantity kind, unit, location and service; the patient is an iot-lite:Entity.
Restricts the range of sosa:resultTime and sosa:phenomenonTime to own transaction-time and valid-time classes; humans and social media are treated as sensors.
Observations link to their monitoring station by an own property (MonitoringStation) rather than through a sensor or feature of interest; SQWRL rules raise pollution alerts over observations.
sosa:Platform is made equivalent to WoR:Environment, and devices and platforms expose Web resources through an own Exposes relation; no observation data shown.
Mobility stations, vehicles and charging columns are themselves sensors; their sensor records bundle a state (SKOS concept), a timestamp and a series of sosa:Observation.
Multi-typing: a musical instrument individual is at once an iot:Thing, mo:Instrument, prov:Entity and sosa:Platform.
Entity-level alignment of a property-graph model: a SensorProperty entity is aligned with ssn:Observation, and an IoT platform with ssn:System.
Instance IRIs are minted under the specification URL (https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-ssn/Sensor{col3}); a toy weather example for table-to-graph mapping.
Quality-of-data indicators are a subclass of ssn:SystemProperty, each with metrics and interpretations, in JSON-LD.
Observations are subclassed by value type (BooleanObservation, DoubleValueObservation), and sensor classes carry axioms fixing what they observe and which observations they make.

The PLC is both a platform hosting sensors and actuators and a system implementing the control procedure, whose input is an observation; attacks compromise features of interest and violate own SafetyProperty nodes.
Jena rules propagate the location of a platform to the subsystems of its deployed system, and shortcut the result chain into an own hasObservationValue.
SSN terms are re-declared in an own ex: namespace (ex:Sensor, ex:observedProperty, ex:onPlatform), with observedProperty on the sensor.
Built on SSN 2011 (ssnx namespace); the observation IRI embeds the indicator and the month (ex:NoiseSensorObservation_LdInterval201704) for a monthly average.
Properties carry the expected value type (semic:observationType / actionType) and static properties hold literal values; sosa:Sensor is split into physical and virtual (software) sensors.
Devices are ssn:System individuals whose continuous behaviour is given by ODE records; variables carry an ssn:symbol property that SSN does not define.
The work mints its own individuals in the ssn: namespace (ssn:AoxMercury, ssn:TVOC).
sosa:madeBySensor is attached to a qudt:Quantity data set in JSON metadata of an HDF5 file, with no sosa:Observation; uncertainty given by qudt:standardUncertainty.
Quality-of-context indicators (precision, freshness) are attached to the sensor output of each observation.
A textbook example in which the device is a platform hosting its sensing element; the observation shown has no sensor or property link.
Reuses SSN 2011 through the Global City Indicator Pollution ontology: concentrations link directly to the weather station by ssn:isProducedBy, keeping raw and calibrated values side by side.
Dataset metadata distinguish the feature of interest (the sample) from the ultimate feature of interest (the sampled real-world phenomenon) of ssn-ext, to support domain-neutral search.

A material sample (sosa:Sample) is the centre of the schema, with a sampling event, a sampling site for the spatial context, curation activities and relations to other resources; a LinkML schema, no RDF instance shown.
The observation module is centred on FeatureOfInterest and ObservationValue (an SSN 2011 class) mixed with SOSA, OWL-Time and OM/QUDT terms.

Sensors are linked to their observations through a hasResult relation, and threshold readings are tied to building components by an own ContainedIn relation; SOSA is aligned rather than reused directly.
Capability attributes take instances or classes as domain and range (unioned with rdfs:Class), revising SSN 2011 measurement capabilities with conditional accuracy.
SSN 2011 terms are paraphrased; features of interest are equated with agricultural conditions (weather, water, soil).
The fused value and its standard deviation go on the result (qudt:standardUncertainty); observations are then translated into logical facts for regulation checking.
Tutorial example: oven temperature observations about a pizza (feature of interest by UUID) with no sensor, property or time triple; the time is in the stream element IRI.
Observations link to the weather station by an own property wep:madeByStation instead of a sensor, and are subclassed (weo:MeteorologicalObservation).
Environmental monitoring stations are modelled as sosa:Sampler and their time series as sosa:Sampling, rather than sensors and observations, with per-pollutant value properties.
Procedures described as plans: EP-Plan plans extend ssn:Procedure (P-Plan lineage) and are aligned with the device (ssn:System) that follows them.
Context attributes (user activity, location, emotion) are made equivalent to sosa:Observation.
